answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust diffuses through bounded-length random walks, so influence decays across edges instead of multiplying among identities. A Sybil cluster resembles karst or shale: dense internally but separated by a sparse external cut and thus low conductance. Cheeger-style bounds limit escape probability and, through min-cut transitivity, cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight; even a lantern seed cannot illuminate beyond that bottleneck.
